crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Satellite Imagery
children.blurb: Satellite imagery as alternative data covers optical, radar, and thermal observations of the Earth's surface collected by public and commercial constellations.

children.name: Card Transaction Data
children.blurb: Card transaction data covers aggregated and anonymized records of consumer purchases made with credit and debit cards, including point of sale, online, and mobile payments.

children.name: Sensor and Shipping Data
children.blurb: Sensor and shipping data covers the digital exhaust of physical movement: vessel positions from AIS, port call records, container and bulk cargo manifests where available, terminal gate and crane activity, truck and rail telematics, and fixed or mobile IoT sensors on assets and in facilities.

children.name: Mobile Location Data
children.blurb: Mobile location data is the record of where a phone or tablet has been, inferred from GPS, Wi-Fi, cell tower and beacon signals.

children.name: Web Data Collection
children.blurb: Web data collection is the practice of gathering information from public websites and web services for use as alternative data.

sections.body: Alternative data is information created for some other purpose, then reused to measure economic or social activity. In artificial intelligence, that usually means feeding satellite images, card transaction records, sensor and shipping feeds, mobile location pings, and web collections into models. Satellite imagery can count cars in parking lots, track construction, monitor crops, or detect industrial activity, while card transaction data can show aggregate spending patterns for a panel of consumers. Sensor and shipping data can reveal port traffic, container volumes, and supply chain movement, and mobile location data can estimate foot traffic. Web data collection can gather prices, job postings, reviews, and other public signals, and AI classifies images, matches records, detects anomalies, and turns messy feeds into time series.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The work stands at a practical but uneven stage. Some tasks are largely solved, such as classifying satellite images, matching records across datasets, and detecting simple anomalies in time series. Other tasks remain hard, including proving that a data panel represents a whole population, handling gaps and source changes, and separating real signal from noise. Privacy rules, terms of service, and data protection law shape what can be collected and used, and the site tracks 149 active AI lawsuits, a reminder that sourcing and use can become contested. Alternative data is often expensive, hard to validate, and uneven across countries and markets, so results may not generalize. The honest limit is that a model can only be as good as the data pipeline behind it, and many pipelines are fragile.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages under this section divide alternative data by source type, moving from physical activity to human movement to digital traces. A reader would go to Satellite Imagery for overhead observation of land, buildings, crops, and industrial sites. Card Transaction Data is the page for consumer spending records and the panel problems that come with them. Sensor and Shipping Data covers physical supply chains, port activity, and container movement. Mobile Location Data covers device pings and foot traffic estimates, with attention to privacy and representativeness. Web Data Collection covers scraping, public listings, prices, and text, and it often supplies the raw material that the other pages depend on.
